cadence.reason: The E4 Motor Inn and all pre-flood machinery are gone; a rope-trimmed lantern-gable Harbor House is rebuilt on seabed ballast.
The General Store lineage returns as a customs-marked loading house with a cargo hoist and wet hawser.
The Claim Office lineage is rebuilt around tide records, a storm-signal mast, and harbor registry pictograms.
The assay role survives through salvage sorting, a roof hoist, sieve, and pearl gauge; the old plant does not.
The chapel identity returns with storm stays, rescue-ring grammar, a tide memorial, and a grounded ballast sill.
The school lineage returns with the required sextant finial, lookout deck, chart board, and rope rails.
The Stamp Mill lineage becomes a timber drydock works with hull cradle, capstan, and hoist.
The Dynamo Hall lineage returns as a crane-and-winch harbor works; no pre-flood generator stack survives.
Wagons do not survive the flood; a waterlogged arrival dinghy is fixed to a weighted seabed cradle.
The horse trough leaves with Chain 1 and is replaced by a sealed freshwater cistern.
Steam, voltage, and motor street hardware is drowned or cannibalized; none is silently mounted in the E5 pack.
Harbor lanterns, a drying-net frame, tide board, and rope-buoy rack announce the submerged working town.
Every heavy house terminates at its canonical ground plane on four compact tarred ballast shoes; the buildings do not float.
The unchanged heritage survivor is carried into the reclaimed town ring and remains independently mounted.
